# vk v0.2.1

Date: 2026-10-20. Status: Experimental Git release.
The workspace owns version 0.2.1 for `vkrust` and `vkrust-gen`. Rust consumers
import the library as `vk`. This Git release does not publish to crates.io.

## API and source

`core` owns all Vulkan and StdVideo ABI declarations, nullable PFNs, cached
dispatch tables and native operations. The crate root re-exports those same
items. `load` opens native libraries and constructs entry dispatch; `memory`
provides the experimental separate-allocation allocator.

Generated families follow the pinned XML declaration order. Handles, records,
unions and aliases share the type declaration sequence; command PFNs and native
operations follow the command sequence. Dispatch tables preserve that order
within each domain. Codec definitions resolve the paired `video.xml` inputs.
An independent XML reader checks source, metadata and generated API-test order.

This checkpoint adds 54 generated native operations covering compute pipeline,
shader, descriptor, resource, copy/barrier, requirements2 and property-query
paths. Both free functions and borrowed methods delegate to one canonical
implementation using cached pointers. Checked slice counts and lengths reject
mismatches before native calls. Requirements2 output chains remain caller-owned.
Pipeline batches preserve non-error native statuses and caller-visible partial
outputs, including on error, so successful partial pipelines can be destroyed.

Rust wrapper constructors use `new` / `new_from_*`; representation conversions
use `from_raw` / `as_raw`. Native creation/allocation/destruction names retain
Vulkan spelling adapted to snake_case. Native cleanup is explicit; Drop never
destroys Vulkan objects, submits or waits. Applications must follow these
experimental API contracts when updating.

## Tests and development

Tests mirror source ownership under `test/rs/{core,load,memory}`. Handwritten
mocks cover forwarding, missing commands, output-chain retention, partial native
failure and invalid lengths. Registry-derived `test_command.gen.rs` checks the
root/core/method signatures and missing-command paths for every admitted recipe.
Those generated checks do not independently prove the ABI or driver semantics.
Generator integration tests exercise freshness, missing/stale source and test
artifacts, repeated generation with unchanged bytes/mtimes, and XML ordering.
No test bodies live in runtime or generator source files.

Dev/test profiles disable incremental compilation and debug information.
The planned native Rust, VMA-derived memory architecture remains a design;
this release does not add pooled allocation or claim VMA equivalence.

## Verification

The release gates cover workspace formatting, strict Clippy, all-feature tests,
default/raw-only feature tests, registry hashes, deterministic generation,
rule synchronization, rustdoc with warnings denied, and verified Cargo packaging.
The squashed release commit is checked before tagging and pushing.

The independent C oracle uses hash-verified Vulkan-Headers
`acbb9391c0a597272800cd3f4363661c00a27c77`. On x86-64 Linux, it verifies
1,447 records and 9,267 layout/value checks, including 348 bitfield byte
comparisons. Toolchain: Rust 1.98.1 / LLVM 22.1.8; GCC 16.2.1.

The explicit native workload creates a shader, descriptors and a compute
pipeline through the public API, dispatches 257 storage-buffer words, waits for
fence completion, invalidates mapped memory and verifies every result before
explicit cleanup. The recorded device is Intel HD Graphics 4400 (HSW GT2),
Mesa 26.2.3-arch1.1, device Vulkan 1.2.354. Mesa reports incomplete Haswell
support. Runtime execution is enabled explicitly with `VULKAN_AVAILABLE=1`.

## Qualification limits

- Exact PFNs/table fields cover the selected 842 registry commands; ergonomic
  functions/methods do not yet cover every command.
- Enabled-version/extension-aware alias admission and lifetime-bearing builders
  remain open. A resolved pointer does not prove a command is enabled.
- ABI evidence is scoped to the recorded target. Protected native-platform
  headers, more architectures and exhaustive scalar/prototype checks remain open.
- Positive VP9 execution, complete decode qualification and separate core,
  synchronization and GPU-assisted validation remain open.
- The allocator provides separate native allocations, not pooled images,
  suballocation, budgets or defragmentation. Non-coherent hardware qualification
  and dedicated-requirements integration remain open.
- No performance superiority, full Vulkan conformance, crates.io publication or
  CI workflow is claimed by this release.
